text:
I've been bringing my two children here for dental care for almost a year now (spending over 20,000 RMB, because their teeth were completely decayed. I initially wanted to give them more control, but now I regret it; the cost of trial and error is too high. You really have to find a balance).

I live in Sansai, which is quite far from here. I came here last year with a doctor, but ended up meeting another doctor, who is also the owner—Dr. Praew.

I've also had my teeth cleaned, filled, and wisdom teeth extracted here. Everyone is very friendly, and I don't have any fear of going to the dentist.

Last Saturday, I suddenly had a lot of pain in my back teeth. Since appointments are required here, I desperately went to a clinic in Sansai. They diagnosed me with root canal treatment, but there was a waiting list. I felt they weren't very professional, so I left.

I called Happy Bear on a whim (because the pain was so bad I wanted immediate help). The receptionist said the appointment was for the next day. Feeling the pain was unbearable, I asked her to ask Dr. Praew what could help alleviate the pain. She said she'd check and get back to me.

A little while later, I received a call from Dr. Praew, who told me to come in that afternoon so they could handle it before they closed. I was so touched.

When I arrived, the doctor said the X-ray taken at the clinic that morning was too blurry and needed to be redone. Everyone was working overtime for me; it was truly heartwarming.

After the X-ray, the doctor examined it and said my pulp was fine and I didn't need root canal treatment, but the periodontal pockets needed cleaning because it had been six months since the last cleaning, and the current pain might be caused by that.

What would have cost over 10,000 baht was resolved for only 460 baht.

It's Thursday today, and after a few days, my toothache has subsided, with only a slight swelling.

Here, I felt the care of friends and the respect shown to patients. I said I didn't want anesthesia, and the doctor supported me. I said I didn't want painkillers, and the doctor prescribed a few just in case.

I would recommend this dental clinic to friends living in Hangdong, but not to those living in Sansai—it's really too far. However, I come regularly, so the distance is acceptable.
